name: Embedding-led candidates, the model picks
description: The quests' own embeddings (vision statement, purpose, category and scope) order the candidates, then the model picks which numbered quests a text is about, or none, and the user's priority orders what is left. quest-backend app/business/quests/quest_selection.py (rank_quest_batch, select_and_rank_quests_for_text before the candidates came from the hybrid ranking); measured by evaluation/components/place_on_a_quest/impls/shared_quest_ranker.py (embedding order, no model) and shared_quest_ranker_model.py (the shipped prompt answered by a model).
advantages: One short prompt and a few output tokens; the model, not a score threshold, says none.
disadvantages: An embedding of the vision statement, purpose, category and scope alone does not see the milestones, state or notes, so a cue that only a milestone phrase resolves is ranked low and falls outside the model's window of 25 quests when an account is large (right quest within the first three: 0.76 on 40 quests, against 0.94 for the hybrid ranking); with no model its pick is always the closest quest, so the first stage can never answer none.

name: Words and meaning candidates, the model picks
description: Candidates ranked by IDF-weighted word overlap over each quest's whole document (vision statement, purpose, category, scope, state, open outcomes, notes, goals, collection entries) plus an embedding bonus from the quest cards, with evidence snippets saying where each match came from; then the model picks which numbered quests the text is about, or none, shown each quest's vision statement and purpose as their own lines under the owner's binding scope. quest-backend app/business/quests/quest_candidates.py (rank_quests_for_message, lexical_rank, semantic_quest_candidates) leads the candidates of quest_selection.select_and_rank_quests_for_text; measured by evaluation/components/place_on_a_quest/impls/hybrid_candidate_ranker.py (no model) and hybrid_candidate_ranker_model.py.
advantages: Sees the words of a quest's milestones and state, so a vague cue reaches the quest that holds it; shows its evidence; the words catch a named quest that embeddings blur.
disadvantages: Reads about six database collections to build the index (cached for a minute per person); without the model its pick is a score floor and a margin, which gives an answer to a message no quest fits when the words happen to overlap.

name: The library judge over the quests it is given
description: The runner's own judge for a runner with no host: the model sees the quests it was handed in the order given and returns the one the message is about (or none) through a tool schema, with the home quest as the default on a failed call. quest_ai_runner/the_intelligence/higher_mind/objectives/quest_judge.py and quest_placement.py.
advantages: Needs no database, embedding or host: the terminal on a folder of quests places a message with it.
disadvantages: No candidate generation, so it sees only the first 25 quests in the order given; the weakest recorded accuracy and the slowest per case.

name: Learn from what is already placed, the model picks
description: The hybrid ranking fused with the similarity-weighted vote of the items the person and their team already put on a quest: AI tasks, goals, goal notes, entries tagged with quests, quest chat turns and measurable outcomes, each a text -> quest example that exists on day one. The most similar are shown to the model after the quests by quest number, a person's correction of a suggestion counts double and an AI-written item half (only where stored), the vote is the answer when the model picks none, and every active quest up to a cap of 40 is shown instead of a window of 25. Items on a team quest are examples for every member who can open it. quest-backend app/business/quests/quest_examples.py, app/services/quest_example_vector_service.py and quest_selection.select_and_rank_quests_for_text; measured offline by evaluation/components/place_on_a_quest/impls/example_vote_ranker.py (no model) and example_vote_ranker_model.py, whose cases may carry optional examples, and on a real account by the quest-backend replay (scripts/checks/quest_placement_replay.py --arm overlay) with a temporal split: only items placed strictly before each case count. Measured on the public cases (model arm) and on one real account's hand-placed AI tasks with labels verified against scopes: the deployed placement, the same code without examples and with examples; the figures are in the results log and the private replay folder.
advantages: A new user is not cold: the examples are the goals, notes and outcomes already on their quests, and a team member inherits the team's history; it corrects siblings whose scopes are close, learns the person's own conventions, and needs no stronger model.
disadvantages: Needs a vector store of placed items (an embedding per item, filled by the daily sync and on task create or move); examples can repeat an earlier wrong placement, so the owner's scope is stated to outrank them; showing ten examples instead of four lowered accuracy, so the prompt shows few.

name: A small learned prior over generic signals
description: A conditional logistic regression over generic per-quest signals the placement already computes (example vote share and best similarity, embedding and hybrid rank, whether the judge picked the quest, home, team quest, priority place), shipped as a small versioned artifact (quest-backend app/data/quest_prior.json, trained by scripts/training/train_quest_prior.py from replay rows; no text, no ids), reordering the candidates and abstaining below a threshold. Opt in with QUEST_PLACEMENT_PRIOR=on. Training rows come from the replay of recorded placements (kept and corrected) and stay in a private folder. Measured on one real account with a time split (train on the earlier cases, test on the later ones) against the same placement without the prior: it matched the judge with examples and did not beat it. A global prior pooled over many users' recorded kept and corrected placements is the way to make it pay: train offline on the pooled rows, evaluate on held-out users and on the public cases, ship the weights as a versioned artifact.
advantages: Cheap (no model call), explicit and inspectable weights, calibrates when to abstain, and can be retrained as placements are recorded.
disadvantages: Trained so far on one account's habits, where the judge and the example vote already carry the signal, so it adds nothing yet; it needs the recorded suggested-versus-final placements of many users to learn what is common.

name: Check the pick against the picked quest's own scope
description: After the model's pick, one more cheap model call is shown ONLY the message, the picked quest in full (scope, vision, purpose) and up to twelve other quests in the fused order, and asked whether the picked quest's own scope excludes the message: it must quote the excluding words, which are checked against the scope in code, and name which listed quest holds the message; a switch is accepted only to a listed quest, and any failure keeps the pick. It targets sibling quests, where the model picks a quest whose own scope says the work is out of scope (a general feature for a quest only for one platform). quest-backend app/business/quests/quest_verify.py and app/prompts/quest_verify_prompts.py, called by quest_selection.select_and_rank_quests_for_text; the QUEST_VERIFY setting picks when it runs: off (the default), disagree (only when the pick is not the example vote's leader) or always. Measured offline by evaluation/components/place_on_a_quest/impls/scope_verify_ranker_model.py and on one real account's hand-placed AI tasks (labels verified against scopes) by the quest-backend replay (scripts/checks/quest_placement_replay.py --arm overlay --verify MODE), each mode against the pick alone on the same cases.
advantages: Cheap when run only on disagreement; it never moves a pick unless the picked quest's written scope excludes the message and another listed quest is named; no per-quest or text rule. Cost: one more call only on the cases where the pick differs from the example vote's leader (about one case in four on the real account); one more on every case in always.
disadvantages: Did not beat the pick alone on one real account's hand-placed AI tasks: a few sibling-quest picks were fixed and about as many correct picks were moved away, within the run to run spread, so a gain is not shown and the accuracy target set for it was not reached (figures: CHANGELOG and the private replay folder). The first wordings of the check moved correct picks to topical neighbours; the required quote and the limit on the quests offered cured most of that. A fast tier model flags catch-all quests as excluded, cannot always find the quest an exclusion line points to by its alias, and ignored a message that names its own destination quest. Selection stays with the pick alone.
